layer_budget_us.notes: single FFN weight pass measured at 306 us (302 MB / ~987 GB/s, at HBM roofline). Second pass costs +210 us.

transport_estimate.method: derived from protocol byte counts and PRINCIPLES 6.6.0 anchors (HCCS peer raw 28 GB/s, W4 put-only aggregate 85.45 GB/s)
transport_estimate.inferred_fixed_overhead_us: ~120-130 per fill, i.e. ~3 sequential doorbell round trips at 20-40 us each
transport_estimate.conclusion: the exposed dispatch fill is latency-dominated, not bandwidth-dominated; reducing sequential round trips matters more than reducing bytes. The INC funnels 4 MB of dispatch egress through one card where native spreads the same traffic across 4 ranks' links in parallel, which is a structural cost of the W+1 topology.

design_deviations_flagged_to_user: Model is Qwen3-30B-A3B (E=128, E_loc=32), not PRINCIPLES 6.2's OLMoE (E=64, E_loc=16). E_loc(32) > live_aic(24) forces the grouped_cube FFN path: GMM1-all -> global barrier -> SwiGLU-all -> global barrier -> GMM2-all, with no per-expert AIC/AIV software pipeline.
activation_waves (W_act) = 1 while PRINCIPLES 2.3 defaults to 2; on the grouped_cube path W_act is inert because SwiGLU already sits between two cohort barriers.

kEnableBulkDenseCombine = true: workers do the FP32 weighted pre-reduce, INC only sums W partials. User relaxed H15 but asked that the main reduction stay INC-side; the weighting currently happens worker-side. User asked that BOTH combine modes be supported and optimized.
serial_shmem hangs at init, so the PRINCIPLES 8.2 2x2 attribution matrix cannot be completed.
PRINCIPLES 6.6.0's D/C micro-benchmark at real message sizes was never run; transport numbers above are inferred, not measured.
user_constraints: token wave must remain the outer loop; every token wave runs its own dispatch, compute and combine. Finer-grained pipelining is allowed only inside a wave.
FFN internals are free to change, subject to robustness, scalability and stability.
no device normalization; wall-clock against the 4-card native baseline is the bar.

rejected_options.merged_two_wave_arena_single_ffn_pass: Ruled out twice: recomputed expected value ranged from -3.9 ms to +1.8 ms because the merged expert-major arena forces the FFN to wait for both waves and removes combine overlap, degenerating to the measured tpw=128 shape (84.6 ms). Also violates the user's rule that every token wave owns its own dispatch/compute/combine.
rejected_options.expert_group_pipelining_as_main_schedule: Would give single-pass weights and overlap simultaneously, but PRINCIPLES 1.2 bans expert-wave as the main scheduler and the user reaffirmed token-wave as the outer loop.

known_issues: serial_shmem mode hangs during init: 'No available shared memory broadcast block', AICore 0%, INC sidecar absent on NPU 12.
aclshmem_putmem_nbi for dispatch relay puts reproducibly hangs with the same shm_broadcast signature; reverted.
IncTraceLine has no per-slot storage, so multi-wave traces overwrite each other within a layer.

fused_inc and native produce different argmax tokens (442 vs 3824), and tpw=128 produces yet another (198); reduction grouping differs per configuration. Synthetic golden is bit-exact, so this is rounding-order sensitivity, not a protocol defect, but it deserves a documented tolerance.
